claims.statement: All Open-Inspect services emit flat JSON log lines with a common envelope: level (debug|info|warn|error), service (web|control-plane|modal-infra|slack-bot, plus the other bot workers), component (sub-area such as router, session-do, bridge, supervisor, handler), msg (a stable event identifier used for querying), and ts (epoch milliseconds); the TypeScript shared logger and the Python sandbox-runtime JSONFormatter produce the same shape, with the runtime emitting its call-site `event` kwarg in the msg/event slot.

The shared TypeScript logger reserves the keys level, component, msg, ts, and service: context and per-call data cannot overwrite them, remaining fields merge base context → child context → per-call data with later values winning, Error values are normalized into error_message/error_stack/error_type/error_code, and JSON.stringify is wrapped in try/catch so an unserializable line degrades to a guaranteed LOG_SERIALIZE_FAILURE event instead of losing the log.

The shared TypeScript logger maps severity to console methods (debug/info → console.log, warn → console.warn, error → console.error) so Cloudflare Workers Logs and tooling see the correct severity while the JSON level field remains available for programmatic filtering.

Each TypeScript service has a thin logger wrapper that pre-binds its service name: control-plane, web, and slack-bot all call the shared createLogger factory with their own SERVICE_NAME constant, so callers only pass a component.

The control-plane CorrelationContext type defines the canonical correlation namespace: trace_id (end-to-end UUID via x-trace-id), request_id (per-hop short UUID via x-request-id), optional session_id and sandbox_id; the Modal client writes these onto provider calls as x-trace-id, x-request-id, x-session-id, x-sandbox-id headers.

Correlation keys are canonically snake_case everywhere outside local in-memory variables (logs: trace_id; HTTP headers: x-trace-id, x-request-id, x-session-id, x-sandbox-id; provider/client objects: correlation.trace_id), and modules that use camelCase internally must convert once at the boundary without mixing casings.

The web service middleware runs on /api/:path*: it accepts a valid inbound x-trace-id (validated against /^[A-Za-z0-9][A-Za-z0-9._:-]{0,127}$/, otherwise generating a fresh UUID), always generates a fresh 8-character hop-local x-request-id (discarding any inbound one), sets the internal x-open-inspect-request-id header, and stamps both x-trace-id and x-request-id onto the response.

Web route code resolves correlation through request-context.ts: traceId from x-trace-id and requestId from the internal x-open-inspect-request-id header minted by middleware; getCorrelationLogFields converts the camelCase pair to trace_id/request_id for log lines and applyCorrelationHeaders writes the wire headers.

Web → control-plane calls forward only x-trace-id alongside the sig1 service auth headers (buildServiceAuthHeaders adds x-trace-id when a traceId is provided); the control plane still generates its own per-hop request_id, so a trace_id spans all services while request_id is hop-local.

The control-plane router builds RequestContext with trace_id taken from the x-trace-id header (fresh UUID fallback) and an 8-character request_id, and every response — including OPTIONS preflights, 404s, and error responses — carries x-request-id and x-trace-id plus CORS headers.

Router → SessionDO hops copy x-trace-id and x-request-id onto every internal DO request via createSessionRuntimeClient, and the DO's SessionHttpDispatcher builds a per-request child logger from those headers without mutating the session-level logger so later callbacks keep their own hop ids.

Modal's FastAPI endpoints accept x_trace_id, x_request_id, x_session_id, and x_sandbox_id headers and stamp them onto the modal.http_request wide event, joining control-plane and sandbox-side logs for the same sandbox; the endpoints also record client-cancelled requests as status 499.

The sandbox runtime bridge connects to wss://{control_plane}/sessions/{session_id}/ws?type=sandbox with Authorization: Bearer {sandbox_token} and X-Sandbox-ID headers, and the supervisor logger binds service=sandbox, sandbox_id, and session_id at boot so sandbox-side events join on sandbox_id/session_id.

The router emits an http.request wide event per incoming HTTP request with http_method, http_path, http_status, duration_ms, outcome, and the RequestMetrics summary (d1_query_count, d1_total_ms, d1_server_total_ms, d1_rows_read, d1_rows_written plus named <name>_ms spans); uncaught handler failures outside HttpError are the only 500 path that logs inside the router.

Prompt runs are visible in three control-plane events: prompt.enqueue (info/warn; outcomes enqueued, deduplicated, conflict on clientRequestId fingerprint mismatch, rejected on queue_full; the message_id is minted here), prompt.dispatch (outcome sent|deferred|send_failed with reason no_sandbox, queue_wait_ms), and prompt.complete (info/warn from the execution_complete handler with outcome success|failure|already_stopped and total/processing/queue durations).

WebSocket admission failures surface as ws.connect warn events with ws_type and reject_reason (sandbox_id_mismatch, token_mismatch, session_terminal, sandbox_stopped, auth_timeout for clients) and successful sandbox connections as ws.connect info with replaced_existing; client auth timeout is logged by the WebSocket manager.

The lifecycle manager emits terminal sandbox wide events: sandbox.spawn and sandbox.restore each log exactly one info/error event with outcome, duration_ms, sandbox_id, provider_object_id, and error; sandbox.snapshot and sandbox.snapshot_saved mark snapshot attempts, sandbox.heartbeat_stale warns on missed heartbeats, sandbox.timeout records inactivity timeouts, and sandbox.spawn_superseded warns when a newer spawn won.

Provider clients emit one wide event per outbound call: modal.request (endpoint, session_id, sandbox_id, http_status, duration_ms, outcome) from the control-plane Modal client, vercel_sandbox.request from the Vercel provider client, and daytona.create_sandbox from the Daytona REST client.

Completion and linear start-callback deliveries emit callback.complete_delivery and callback.started_delivery (info/error) with session_id, message_id, source, outcome, attempts, retries, http_status, and reject_reason, plus per-attempt *_attempt_failed warns during retries.

Image builds use one image_build.* vocabulary across component image-builds:* and router:image-builds, with scope_kind (repo|environment) and scope_id; key events are image_build.build_triggered, build_complete_received, build_failed, callback_auth_failed (warn), finalization_job_invalid (error), finalization_error (error; retries exhaust to the DLQ), scheduler_tick plus scheduler phase warnings, trigger_error, late_artifact_recorded, save_hook_trigger(_failed), secrets_change_superseded, toggle, cleanup, and stale_marked.

The modal-infra sandbox manager logs provider-side lifecycle events sandbox.create, sandbox.snapshot, and sandbox.restore (info) with sandbox_id, modal_object_id, snapshot_image_id, repo_owner, repo_name, duration_ms, and outcome, plus sandbox.create_build for image builds.

The sandbox supervisor logs sandbox.startup (info; repo_owner/repo_name, boot_mode, restored_from_snapshot, from_repo_image, git_sync_success, setup_success, start_success, opencode_ready, duration_ms, outcome), supervisor.start, supervisor.error (unhandled exception), and supervisor.fatal (the sandbox will exit and the fatal error is POSTed to /sessions/:id/sandbox-error); OpenCode crashes emit opencode.crash with exit_code and restart_count.

The bridge process emits bridge.connect (outcome and aggregate connection counters), bridge.disconnect (reason, ws_close_code, connection_duration_seconds, total_connected_duration_seconds, reconnect counters), bridge.reconnect (attempt, delay_s), and bridge.run_complete; connection errors matching HTTP 401/403/404/410 are considered fatal and not retried — the bridge exits gracefully so the control plane can spawn or restore a sandbox.

Prompt processing inside the sandbox emits prompt.start (message_id, model, reasoning_effort), prompt.run (message_id, model, outcome, duration_ms), and prompt.error (message_id, exc), plus prompt.invalid_attachments and prompt.no_output when OpenCode finished without emitting assistant output.

Git and OpenCode operations in the sandbox log git.clone_start/clone_complete/clone_error, git.sync_complete, git.push_start/push_complete/push_error, opencode.session.ensure (opencode_session_id, action), opencode.start/ready/crash, opencode.restart (delay_s, restart_count), and opencode.max_restarts.

The slack-bot mints a fresh trace_id at the /events and /interactions edge, logs http.request per webhook (info/warn; outcome rejected with reject_reason invalid_signature on bad signatures), deduplicates events through KV with slack.event.duplicate (debug) and slack.event.dedupe_unavailable (error, degraded mode), and logs control_plane.create_session and control_plane.send_prompt with trace_id, session_id, message_id, http_status, duration_ms, and outcome.

Slack attachment problems use the slack.attachment.* warn family (untrusted_url, download_failed, download_error, size_rejected, too_large, upload_failed, upload_error, notify_failed, file_lookup_failed) and media delivery uses slack.media.*; size events enforce a 10 MiB per-image cap and the bot forwards at most six images per message, with a text-plus-image request losing images still running the text and attempting an in-thread warning.

scripts/cf-logs.ts queries the Cloudflare Workers Observability Telemetry Query API (POST /accounts/{id}/workers/observability/telemetry/query) with filters on the application session_id field, $metadata.requestId, $metadata.traceId (fetch events only), $metadata.message free-text (populated from msg or message), level, and $workers.scriptName; it requires CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN (Workers:Read) and CLOUDFLARE_ACCOUNT_ID, defaults to a 30-minute lookback and 1000-event limit, supports --json raw output for LLM debugging, and application fields live under source (source.level, source.service, source.component, source.msg/source.message, source.ts) rather than at the top level.

Redaction rules forbid authorization headers, HMAC tokens derived from MODAL_API_SECRET and sig1 signatures derived from per-service SERVICE_AUTH_SECRETs, GitHub App private keys/installation tokens, GitHub OAuth tokens, and sandbox auth tokens; body content is omitted unless explicitly whitelisted and truncated.

Log level guidelines are debug for high-frequency internals (heartbeats, cache), info for wide events, warn for degraded-but-recoverable, and error for failures requiring investigation; LOG_LEVEL env var controls the minimum per service, parsed by parseLogLevel with an allowlist defaulting to info.

Error fields are uniform across TypeScript and Python services: error_type (error class name), error_message, error_stack (error level only, truncated to the last 2000 characters on the Python side), and error_code when the error carries a string code.

Wide events classify results with an outcome field: success (completed normally), error (failed with an error), rejected (denied before processing — auth, validation), timeout, and cancelled (cancelled by caller).

The SessionDO wraps its logger with createSessionScopedLogger, which injects session_id into every emitted line through a latched resolver so the id upgrades the moment /internal/init writes the session row, without pinning the Durable Object id that existed during first activation.
